figures.title: Study and evidence map
figures.subtitle: Question groups define the evidence units; additional fits do not add questions.
figures.caption: Figure 1. Study and evidence map. The primary learner, later controls, and post-hoc same-question diagnostics reuse 50 question groups. The separate two-solver panel has 64 groups; the cap cohort contains 11 of those same questions. The fresh guard panel uses 228 questions disjoint from development and evaluates a policy contrast with a common cutoff refitted on all 128 development states and frozen before fresh collection. Dashed arrows show design influence, not independent replication or pooled evidence. Boxes are not proportional to sample size.

figures.title: Recorded utility contrasts
figures.subtitle: Average of A4 to B4 and B4 to A4; the same 50 question groups in both panels.
figures.caption: Figure 2. Recorded averaged four-draw utility contrasts on the same 50 questions. Panel A compares the original combined Ridge learner with a baseline selected within training from accept, escalate, and confidence. Panel B compares three families selected within training with the four-draw confidence policy; the other individual policy results remain in Table 3. Bars are the recorded conditional 90% whole-question bootstrap intervals with fits and actions fixed. They omit refitting and research-selection uncertainty and do not provide joint coverage. Different comparators and reused data prevent a pooled effect or common causal interpretation. All displayed progression screens failed.

figures.title: Two-solver diagnostic: accuracy and output cost
figures.subtitle: 64 shared question groups; 128 paired states per solver; two draws per mode.
figures.caption: Figure 3. Two-solver diagnostic, averaged across the two draw directions. Every policy point uses 128 paired states in the same 64 question groups. Accuracy and token values are transcribed point estimates; no uncertainty interval is inferred for these marks. Escalation pays for the direct draft plus thinking, including inserted closure tokens. The labels 4/64 and 24/64 count questions with positive realized utility gain in at least one of two draws at lambda=.05. These counts depend on the draw count and do not identify positive expected gain. Output tokens are not equal compute units across solver sizes; no cross-size latency or energy advantage is established.
